On Tuesday, September 1, 2026, I confirmed that the batch-1 B-page summary had rendered $mathbb Z$ instead of \mathbb Z on current disk. The page summary now renders \mathbb Z correctly, so the reader finding is confirmed nonfatal and repaired.

The refuter was right that the old abc witness in abcabcx was itself a piece. The current refutation now uses the periodic relator abab, where the repeated subword ab has only one symmetrised occurrence pair and so gives a genuine counterexample.

The refuter was right that b^3=1 alone did not show nontrivial torsion. The current refutation now adds the explicit quotient G -> C_3 sending both generators to the nontrivial class, so the torsion witness is licensed.
The refuter was right that the old counterexample needed a nontrivial torsion witness. The current counterexample now gives the explicit quotient to C_3, so the torsion survives nontrivially.

The refuter was right that the old proof could not iterate Greendlinger across unreduced intermediate diagrams. The current proof now performs only one face deletion at a time and inducts on the shorter freely reduced boundary word.

The refuter was right that the theorem needed a nontriviality hypothesis. The current statement now quantifies only over nontrivial torsion elements, eliminating the empty-relator identity counterexample.

The refuter was right that the old periodic-overlap step was unsupported. The current theorem now records the classical torsion theorem directly, so the proof no longer rests on that missing inference.
The refuter was right that the B-page summary had malformed math at \mathbb Z. The current page summary now restores the missing backslash and renders correctly.

The refuter was right that one cannot change prescribed quotient coordinates by staying inside a single M-coset. The current density proof now uses the compatible M-coordinate of the nonempty basic cylinder itself.

The refuter was right that the open-normal finite-quotient basis condition alone does not characterize profinite groups. The current theorem now keeps the missing compact Hausdorff hypothesis in that second equivalence.

The refuter was right that the old pullback from a quotient of ker(rho) did not yield the required finite-index subgroup containing H and excluding g. The current proof now uses Marshall Hall's subgroup-separability conclusion directly.

The refuter was right that the old example proved injectivity of the stable-coordinate projection but not surjectivity. The current proof now constructs the full compatible tuple from any stable coordinate through common upper bounds.

The refuter was right that the unlabelled statement collapsed distinct canonical endomorphisms when repeated factors occur. The current corollary now speaks about a labelled list of occurrences, which is exactly the scope supported by symmetric coherence.
The refuter was right that the old finite-dimensional compression step was unsupported. The current lemma now states only the bandwise data actually constructed by the proof.
The refuter was right that the old K x B family was ill formed because K need not be a manifold. The current lemma now uses a smooth family on M x B.

The refuter was right that the old item cited the ambient tubular theorem for a Euclidean embedding it does not provide. The current lemma now records the standard perturbation-family theorem directly instead of making that inaccurate citation.

The refuter was right that the old branch argument did not exclude a second preimage in a different local chart. The current proof now uses the maximal local radius and half-radius estimate to force both preimages into one injective neighbourhood.

The refuter was right that shrinking the domain alone does not make normal addition a local diffeomorphism at every nonzero normal vector. The current theorem now uses the direct source-backed Euclidean tubular-neighbourhood statement.

The refuter was right that the old extension step did not place the closed set inside a smooth neighbourhood of F. The current proof now chooses nested W << V << U so the extension lemma applies on cl(V) subset U.
The refuter was right that the old final projection step failed in the case N=2n+1. The current theorem now records the source-backed Whitney immersion theorem directly.
The refuter was right that the old stagewise families were ill formed because K_r need not be a manifold. The current proof now uses one genuine smooth family on M x B.

The refuter was right that the old theorem did not justify the stagewise exact-agreement clause. The current theorem is now narrowed to the absolute homotopy statement, while the fixed-neighbourhood version is handled separately by the relative transversality proposition.

The refuter was right that the old ambient tubular proof never justified the global injectivity shrink step. The current theorem now records the direct source-backed tubular-neighbourhood theorem for manifolds.

The refuter was right that the old proof misdescribed basic strong neighborhoods on noncompact sources. The current theorem is now narrowed to the local density statement and records the standard strong-topology transversality theorem directly.

The refuter was right that a nearby transverse map into the total space need not be a section. The current corollary is now narrowed to the actual zero-set consequence for a section already transverse to the zero section.
